finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined to /srv/files with no containment check. filepath.Join only cleans the path, so `../` sequences climb out of the root. An unauthenticated attacker can read any file the process can access.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (files.go:12), unauthenticated
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered with no auth middleware
name = r.URL.Query().Get("f") is attacker-controlled and unvalidated
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", which escapes root
The file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No prefix or containment check, no rejection of `..` or absolute paths, no symlink resolution, and no auth on the route. Join does not neutralize traversal because it cleans `..` segments lexically, which lets them climb above root. The /avatar handler is not affected because filepath.Base strips directory components.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name), which only cleans the path, so "../../etc/passwd" resolves to /etc/passwd. The route at files.go:32 has no auth, and files.go:18 writes the file contents to the response.
